title: Taught words are never too hard
statement: Don't mark a word as too hard when the material teaches it, and fail reading level only on several untaught words or constructions that are off-level.
example: One script rubric fails reading level only when 3 or more off-grade words or constructions are not being taught.
detail: Guards against false failures in the evaluator's script rubric say that words a script explicitly defines and teaches are always grade-appropriate, whatever their difficulty (`shadow/bench/src/inceptbench/prompts/video_script/evaluation.txt` line 360). The judge may not fail reading level without citing at least 3 specific off-grade words or constructions, and they must not be ones the script teaches (lines 92 and 364). The short-answer rubric says the same of curriculum terms being explicitly taught (`question/scr_evaluation.txt` line 127).

evidence.quote: Words being explicitly defined and taught in the script are always grade-appropriate regardless of difficulty — that is the point of the video.
- Do not fail reading_age_fit without citing at least 3 specific words or constructions that are clearly off-grade
**Fail:** 3 or more words or constructions are clearly above or below grade level AND are not being taught as new vocabulary in the script.
curriculum terms being explicitly taught are always allowed.
